title: Dadhikrāvan: may he make our mouths fragrant

sandhi_exceptions.note: दधिक्राव्णः + अकारिषम्: -aḥ becomes -o and the following a is kept, not elided — a Vedic hiatus inside the pāda (P. 6.1.115 (प्रकृत्याऽन्तःपादमव्यपरे)).

words.role: object of praise, governed by akāriṣam
words.context: Bhāskara derives the name as ‘he who goes to the offerings’ («तानि क्रामति गच्छतीति दधिक्रावा अग्निः») and takes him as Agni in the form of a horse

words.meaning: I have made (praise), I have celebrated
words.role: main verb of the first line
words.context: Bhāskara: «करोतेश्छान्दसो लुङ्», the i being a Vedic insertion («छान्दस इकारोपजनः»)

words.gram: adj., n. acc. pl. (Vedic, ending dropped)

words.role: belongs with tāriṣat: pra tāriṣat ‘may he lengthen’

words.gram: pers. pron., 1st pl., gen. (enclitic; pada form नः)
words.context: after pra the n becomes ṇ; Bhāskara: «उपसर्गाद्बहुलम्» … «नसो णत्वम्»

sandhi.rule: final m before a consonant becomes the nasal of that consonant’s class

samasa.meaning: the one who goes to (or strides over) the offerings

morphology.note: the Vedic neuter plural in -ā for -āni.
नः, ‘our’, written with ṇ after the preverb pra, as the recited text has it.
the iṣ-aorist of √कृ, which in classical Sanskrit has the s-aorist akārṣam.

translation.literal: I have made (praise) of Dadhikrāvan, the victorious, swift horse; may he make our mouths fragrant, may he prolong our lives.
translation.readable: I have sung the praise of Dadhikrāvan, the victorious, swift horse: may he make our mouths sweet, and lengthen our lives.

meaning: A single anuṣṭubh to Dadhikrāvan, the divine horse of the Ṛgveda, who stands for the swift morning power that sets the world going; Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara reads him as Agni in the form of a horse. The worshipper says that he has praised him, and asks two things: that the mouth be made fragrant — fit to speak holy words — and that life be lengthened. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (1.5.11.4) it is the invitatory verse of an offering of rice to Dadhikrāvan (Bhāskara’s viniyoga); in the Ṛgveda it is 4.39.6. It opens the second sprinkling of the Sandhyāvandanam, before the three ṛks to the Waters are said again.
in_the_rite: Punar-mārjana (the second sprinkling), in all three services: water is sprinkled with dadhikrāvṇo and then with āpo hi ṣṭhā and the vyāhṛtis. The Mylapore prayoga gives the viniyoga: Vāmadeva the seer, anuṣṭubh the metre, the All-gods (or Dadhikrāvan) the deity (vin-dadhikravnah).

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara explains the name: the offerings that hold (dadhi) are what he goes to, «तानि क्रामति गच्छतीति दधिक्रावा अग्निः» — Dadhikrāvan is Agni, who took the form of a horse. ‘I have made’ means ‘I am his worker in the rite’: «कर्मकरस् स्यामिति यावत्». The second line asks for fragrance won by good deeds — «अस्मत्सुकृतसमृद्ध्या समासादित-सौरभ्याणि» — and long life, «आयूंषि च प्रतारिषत् प्रवर्धयतु».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: In the Saṃhitā the verse is the invitatory (puronuvākyā) of the offering to Dadhikrāvan in a three-offering rite: «दधिक्राव्ण्णे चरुम्», «दधिकाव्ण्ण इत्यनुष्टुप्».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Anuṣṭubh: four pādas of eight syllables. The Ṛgveda (4.39.6) has the same words; the Taittirīya writes the doubled ṇ of its tradition (दधिक्राव्ण्णो).

notes.label: historical
notes.text: Dadhikrāvan is praised in four hymns of the fourth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda (4.38–40) as a divine racehorse; this verse closes the second of them.
